html:
A trading town on the Cacheu River, founded as a Portuguese post in 1588, one of the earliest European bases in West Africa and the first centre of Portuguese Guinea.

Luso-African traders, called lancados, settled among local peoples and bought captives, wax and ivory, many sent to Cape Verde and on to the Americas. Cacheu was a major port of the Atlantic slave trade in the 17th century, supplied in part by Kaabu. Later Bissau overtook it. Its small fort survives, and a memorial museum to the slave trade opened there in 2016.
